images.prompt:

The face inclines diagonally upwards and eyes look gently up; chin lifts only moderately, with natural continuous neck anatomy. This is a clearly visible comfortable endpoint, not an extreme backward head bend; do not look straight at the ceiling.
Keep everything else exactly as in image 1: same facial identity, head size, black ponytail, white short-sleeved shirt, dark charcoal trousers, chair and chair location, torso upright naturally and not arching backwards, shoulders relaxed and at the exact same height, both hands on thighs at the exact same positions. The chair back remains below shoulder level and does not touch the neck. No hand on forehead or head. Match canvas dimensions 1536x1024 landscape, camera, crop, woman scale, gray-blue background and soft lighting. Complete head, hair, shoulders, torso and lap hands visible as before.
Exactly one woman and one pose. No text, numbers, arrows, collage, border, motion ghosts or watermark. Preserve natural skin and fabric texture and realistic anatomy.

images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: one photorealistic rehabilitation exercise demonstration photo, action 149 T-AXU-011 step s01 neutral setup.
Input images: all three supplied reference images are identity, wardrobe, photographic lighting and gray-blue background references only. Use exactly this same East Asian adult woman, same age, face, skin tone, natural proportions, black ponytail, plain white short-sleeve T-shirt and dark charcoal gray trousers. Do not copy the arm gestures of references.
Primary request: a front-facing seated neutral head position for gentle neck movement. She sits stably and naturally upright on a simple gray armless chair. Chest and face point straight toward the camera. Head is precisely upright, nose centered, chin level, eyes look straight forward. Both ears and shoulder relationships are clear. Shoulders are relaxed, naturally dropped, at equal height. Both arms hang relaxed and BOTH complete hands rest palm-down separately on their corresponding thighs just above knees. Fingers natural and readable.
Composition/framing: a single 3:2 horizontal image, approximately 1536 by 1024 pixels. Fixed centered frontal camera at upper chest/head level, natural portrait lens perspective. Show entire head including ponytail, both shoulders, upper torso, both elbows, both forearms, both complete hands, knees/upper thighs and visible gray chair edges/back cues. Frame from modest margin over head down to just below knees. No full legs are needed. Her head and neck must be large enough to clearly teach a small neck movement. Plenty of unobtrusive background to both sides.
Style/medium: realistic reference-matched studio photograph, soft gray-blue seamless background and soft natural studio light, crisp anatomy and fine fabric/hair texture. Calm mild pleasant expression, mouth closed.
Constraints: one woman, one posture, no head rotation, no side bend, no neck extension or flexion, no shoulder shrug, no trunk lean. No text, numbers, arrows, logos, watermark or picture panels. This is the shared neutral reference for later side bending and head rotation; keep pose visibly symmetric.
images.qa_observation: 实看验收通过：女性身份、白短袖深灰裤、马尾、灰蓝背景及柔和棚拍光线与三参考一致；正面坐稳，头中立平视、鼻尖朝前，双肩水平自然下垂，胸口朝前；完整头部、双肩、上身、双臂、双手、膝上及灰椅线索清楚；手指与关节连续，未见可辨畸形；无字无箭头。

images.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: one photorealistic rehabilitation step demonstration, action 151 T-AXU-013, step 02, gentle seated chin retraction.
Input image: the attached seated side-profile photograph is the sole edit target. Preserve its person, identity, hairstyle/ponytail, white T-shirt, black trousers, gray backed chair, relaxed shoulders, trunk, hands on thighs, seat contact, camera, exact framing, dimensions 1536x1024, light and blue-gray background.
Change ONLY the head and its local neck transition: the whole head slides horizontally backward toward the left of the image by a small 1–2 cm, while the face continues looking to the right with eyes at approximately the same horizontal level. This is cervical retraction, a tiny horizontal chin glide; the chin makes a small soft double-chin fold. Keep the nose and eye direction essentially horizontal, preserving approximately the original head orientation. Ear, nose, jaw and whole skull translate posteriorly together; do not rotate the face downward or upward. The movement is gentle and barely a little visible, with a naturally proportioned comfortable neck.
Keep the entire crown, ponytail and shoulders in frame. The back continues resting naturally by the same chair back; never press the head against a wall or forcefully into a chair. Keep shoulders lowered and trunk completely unchanged. One posture, no text, no arrows, no diagrams, no ghost outlines, no split panels, no new props. Avoid neck flexion, nodding, bowing the head, looking down, looking up, exaggerated chin tucking, overcompression or extreme head retraction.
